sourcePolicy: Only official university undergraduate admissions pages are accepted.

records.fact: Harvey Mudd requires international applicants to demonstrate English proficiency. Accepted evidence includes Duolingo 130 on the 160-point scale, TOEFL iBT/Home/Paper 100, IELTS Academic 7.5, Cambridge C1 190, or Cambridge C2 200. The requirement may be waived after application review when the school uses English as its primary language of instruction.

Villanova requires all international undergraduate students to submit proof of English proficiency. The official first-year page accepts Cambridge English, Duolingo, IELTS, Pearson PTE, and TOEFL iBT; the requirement may be waived when English is native or when the applicant has completed more than three consecutive years of secondary schooling where English is the primary language of instruction. The current page does not publish a universal minimum score.

UC Santa Cruz requires international first-year applicants whose schooling was not sufficiently English-medium to demonstrate English competency. The official page lists IELTS 6.5, TOEFL iBT 4.5 on the current scale, Duolingo 115, and specified AP/IB, ACT, SAT, or UC-transferable English-course alternatives.

The University of Delaware requires English-proficiency evidence for direct international undergraduate admission. Its official table lists TOEFL iBT 79 before January 21, 2026 or 4 afterward, IELTS 6.5, TOEFL Essentials 8, Duolingo 110+, Cambridge B2 First/171, and pathway thresholds for applicants who need additional English preparation.

SMU requires official English-proficiency scores for first-year applicants whose language of instruction is bilingual or not solely English, with some waiver cases. The official international checklist confirms SMU accepts TOEFL, IELTS, and Duolingo; the undergraduate process page identifies the same submission requirement but does not publish a universal minimum score there.

The University of Pittsburgh's official admissions policy requires international undergraduate applicants to demonstrate English proficiency unless an exemption applies. The policy lists TOEFL iBT 80 or PBT 550 and IELTS 6.5 as baseline evidence; individual academic units may require higher proficiency, and scores below TOEFL iBT 100 or IELTS 7.0 may lead to an additional English assessment after admission.

UC Riverside requires international first-year applicants to demonstrate English proficiency. Its official page lists IELTS Academic 6.5 or higher and recognizes AP/IB English results as alternative benchmarks; the page also directs applicants to the UC-wide English-proficiency requirements for the complete set of accepted evidence.

UIC requires international first-year applicants to submit English-proficiency scores when required by the applicant's prior-study country, or qualify for an exemption. UIC accepts TOEFL iBT, IELTS Academic, PTE Academic, and Duolingo English Test for the applicable undergraduate process; the official requirements page says score validity is two years and country-specific requirements determine whether scores are required.

Clemson requires international applicants to submit English-proficiency evidence through Duolingo, TOEFL, or IELTS, with waivers available when English is the primary or an official language. The official undergraduate international application page also describes conditional admission for academically admissible applicants who do not initially meet the university's English requirements, but does not publish a universal minimum score on the reviewed page.

UMass Amherst requires non-native English speakers to demonstrate English proficiency. For first-year applicants it lists Duolingo 115, TOEFL 80 before January 21, 2026 or 4.5 afterward, IELTS Academic 6.5, or Cambridge English 176, with stated section minimums for several tests; verified waiver paths include qualifying English-medium schooling and are not automatic.

GW requires official English-proficiency scores when English is not the applicant's first language. The undergraduate admissions page lists TOEFL 90 before January 26, 2026 or 4.5 afterward, IELTS 6.5, PTE Academic 61, or Duolingo 120; higher scores may waive English for Academic Purposes coursework, and published waiver criteria also include qualifying SAT/ACT performance.

Tulane requires English proficiency for admission when the applicant is not a native English speaker. The official page lists typical successful-applicant scores of TOEFL 95+, IELTS 6.5+, or Duolingo 130+, and states that SAT Evidence-Based Reading and Writing 600+ or ACT English 27+ can waive the English-proficiency score requirement; some English-official-language study may also qualify for a waiver.

The University of Miami requires non-native English speakers applying internationally to submit TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo English Test results, generally valid for two years. The official undergraduate policy reviewed describes waiver routes for demonstrated English proficiency and conditional admission, but does not publish a universal minimum score in that source.

William & Mary's official undergraduate international-applicant guidance says students whose native language is not English and whose recent schooling was not in English should strongly consider TOEFL or IELTS Academic; Duolingo is also accepted when TOEFL/IELTS are unavailable. The page describes this as strongly recommended rather than a universal published minimum-score requirement.

UC Merced requires international applicants to demonstrate English proficiency. The official page lists TOEFL iBT 80, IELTS Academic 6.5, or Duolingo English Test 115; it also accepts specified SAT/ACT, AP, and IB English evidence for eligible first-year applicants. Language scores must not be more than two years old.

NC State requires international first-year applicants to provide proof of English proficiency, subject to listed country exemptions. For full undergraduate admission, the official page lists TOEFL iBT 80 before January 21, 2026 or 4.5 on/after that date, IELTS Academic 6.5, Duolingo 110, PTE 58, and TOEFL Essentials 9.0, with conditional-admission thresholds also published separately.

International undergraduate applicants to UNC-Chapel Hill whose first language is not English must submit English-proficiency test scores. UNC accepts TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo, and Cambridge exams; the official catalog lists typical strong-applicant scores of TOEFL 100, IELTS Academic 7.5, Duolingo 130, or Cambridge C1 185, and explicitly says these are not minimums.

Wake Forest requires an English-proficiency score from international undergraduate applicants whose first language is not English and/or whose school is not taught in English. The official page accepts TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo and does not publish a universal minimum score on the reviewed page.

Virginia Tech requires applicants whose native language is not English to demonstrate proficiency. Its international-admissions page accepts TOEFL, IELTS, PTE, Duolingo, and Cambridge options; the published thresholds include TOEFL iBT 80 with no subsection below 16, IELTS 6.5 with no subscore below 6.5, PTE 59, Duolingo 115, and Cambridge 176, with the page also listing updated TOEFL-scale requirements for newer exams.

Florida State University requires official English-proficiency results from international applicants whose native language is not English. Minimum undergraduate scores listed by FSU are TOEFL iBT 80 before January 21, 2026, TOEFL iBT 4.0 on or after January 21, 2026, IELTS Academic 6.5, PTE 55, Michigan Language Assessment 55, Duolingo 125, or Cambridge C1/C2 180.

International freshman applicants to the University of South Carolina must demonstrate English proficiency unless an official exemption applies. The university lists TOEFL iBT 77, TOEFL paper 550, IELTS 6.5, PTE 53, Duolingo English Test 115, SAT Evidence-Based Reading and Writing 560, or ACT English 22 as minimum options; conditional admission through English Programs for Internationals may be available.

International freshman applicants to The University of Texas at Austin must submit TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo English Test scores unless an official exemption applies. The published minimums are TOEFL iBT 79, IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, or Duolingo English Test 115.

International first-year applicants to the University of Washington must submit an official English-proficiency score. The current page lists TOEFL iBT 76 for tests before January 21, 2026, TOEFL iBT 4.0 effective January 21, 2026, IELTS 6.0, or Duolingo English Test 110 as minimum scores.

WashU requires evidence of English-language proficiency for international undergraduate applicants for whom English is a second language, using TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo English Test; the official admissions material reviewed does not publish a universal minimum score in that source.

For undergraduate applicants, the University of Chicago lists an English proficiency examination such as TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo as optional application material; the official application materials do not state a universal minimum English-test score requirement.

International undergraduate applicants must demonstrate English proficiency before enrolling. CU Boulder lists TOEFL iBT 80 for tests taken before January 2026, TOEFL iBT 4.0 for tests taken after January 2026, IELTS 6.5, Cambridge 180, PTE Academic 58, and Duolingo English Test 115 among the qualifying options; approved prior study can also satisfy the requirement.

International undergraduate applicants must demonstrate English proficiency. The University of Iowa lists TOEFL iBT 80 before January 2026 with section minimums of 17, TOEFL iBT 4.0 after January 2026 with section minimums of 3.5, TOEFL Home Edition 80 with section minimums of 17, TOEFL Essentials 9, and IELTS 6.5 with all subscores at least 6.0 for admission; lower subscores can trigger additional ESL coursework.
Stanford does not require an English proficiency exam for undergraduate admission. Applicants may self-report scores if they wish; English fluency is a prerequisite for admission.

MIT strongly recommends an English proficiency exam for non-native English speakers who have used English for fewer than five years or do not speak English at home or school. MIT lists minimum and recommended scores for accepted exams.

Yale requires non-native English speakers who have not completed at least two years of secondary education in English to submit an accepted English proficiency test. Applicants with at least two years of English-medium secondary education are exempt from that requirement.
Harvard does not require first-year or transfer applicants to take an English proficiency exam, but applicants may submit TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo scores for review.

Princeton requires TOEFL, IELTS Academic, Duolingo English Test, or PTE Academic when English is not the applicant's native language and the secondary school language of instruction is not English. Applicants with at least three years of English-medium secondary education are exempt.

Brown requires admitted international students to demonstrate English proficiency and recommends an English proficiency test for applicants whose first language, home language, or secondary-school instruction is not English. Brown lists TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo, Pearson, and Cambridge English among accepted tests.

Penn exempts applicants from an English proficiency test when English is their native language or was the primary language of instruction for at least three years. Otherwise, Penn requires official TOEFL, IELTS Academic, or Duolingo English Test scores for international undergraduate applicants.

Duke recommends, but does not require, an English proficiency test for non-native English speakers or students not studying in an English-medium curriculum. Duke accepts Cambridge, Duolingo, IELTS Academic, PTE Academic, and TOEFL results.

Cornell recognizes English as demonstrated by native language, U.S. citizenship or permanent residence, or four years of English-medium instruction. Applicants who do not meet those criteria must submit an English proficiency exam; Cornell lists TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo, and Cambridge exams with score guidance.

Dartmouth requires applicants whose first language is not English and whose curriculum has not been delivered in English for at least two years to submit an English proficiency exam score. Accepted exams include TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo, and Cambridge English.

Northwestern requires official English proficiency scores when an applicant's first or primary language is not English or secondary schooling has not been in English. Northwestern accepts Duolingo, IELTS, and TOEFL and does not set a minimum score.

UConn requires standardized English proficiency results for international applicants whose primary language is not English. Its undergraduate policy lists TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo, LanguageCert Academic, and PTE Academic, with waiver categories for qualifying applicants.

The University of Michigan requires non-native English speakers to demonstrate English proficiency for undergraduate admission consideration. The official policy lists TOEFL, IELTS, ECPE, CAE/CPE, PTE Academic, and MET, with specified score ranges and exemptions.

UC Berkeley requires international applicants to demonstrate English proficiency. Accepted routes include TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo, qualifying AP or IB English results, qualifying ACT/SAT English results, or at least three years of English language of instruction.

UCLA considers applicants proficient when all secondary education was completed in English. Otherwise, applicants with less than three years of English instruction must demonstrate proficiency through TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo; UCLA publishes competitive score guidance.

USC requires international applicants whose native language is not English to demonstrate English proficiency. USC lists TOEFL, IELTS, Cambridge, PTE, SAT/ACT English, and Duolingo alternatives with published minimums and conditions.

Rice requires applicants whose first language is not English to demonstrate proficiency either through at least two years of full-time English-language curriculum or an approved exam. Rice lists TOEFL, IELTS Academic, Cambridge, and Duolingo with minimum scores.

Notre Dame requires English proficiency testing when an applicant's primary first language is not English or secondary education was not primarily in English. It accepts TOEFL, IELTS, PTE Academic, and Duolingo, with SAT/ACT waiver conditions.

Emory requires international applicants whose primary language is not English to demonstrate English proficiency. The official admissions pages identify TOEFL, IELTS, and Duolingo as English-proficiency routes and distinguish optional interviews from the testing requirement.

Vanderbilt requires proof of English proficiency for international applicants even while SAT/ACT submission is optional for the current application cycles. Its undergraduate admissions testing policy treats English-proficiency testing separately from general standardized testing.

Georgia Tech requires international applicants to demonstrate English proficiency under University System of Georgia approved methods. The official undergraduate page distinguishes this requirement from optional supplementary materials such as Duolingo, InitialView, and Vericant.

The University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign requires international applicants to demonstrate English proficiency. Depending on curriculum and ACT/SAT submission, applicants must submit TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo, or qualifying ACT/SAT evidence under the university's published conditions.

UVA strongly encourages applicants whose first language is not English to submit English-language assessment results. UVA accepts TOEFL, IELTS, Cambridge, and Duolingo results and also considers InitialView or Vericant evaluations.

Boston University requires international students to submit English proficiency testing as the primary means of evaluating English ability. Its undergraduate admissions page lists TOEFL, IELTS, and Duolingo and publishes competitive score guidance.

Northeastern requires all first-year and transfer applicants to demonstrate English proficiency. It accepts Cambridge, Duolingo, IELTS Academic, PTE Academic, and TOEFL, with waiver options based on the instructional language of prior study.

Tufts requires applicants whose primary language is not English to submit proof of English proficiency unless they completed at least three years in a secondary school where English was the primary language. Tufts accepts TOEFL, IELTS, PTE, and Duolingo.

Purdue evaluates English proficiency for international undergraduate applicants whose first language is not English. It accepts Duolingo, IELTS, TOEFL, ACT, and SAT evidence and publishes minimum scores and score-age rules.

Ohio State requires official proof of English language skills for international undergraduate applicants. It accepts approved TOEFL, IELTS, ACT, Duolingo, or SAT evidence, with alternate exemptions based on U.S. schooling or approved citizenship/degree locations.

UW–Madison requires English proficiency evidence for international undergraduate applicants unless an approved waiver applies. The official policy lists Duolingo, IELTS Academic, and TOEFL iBT minimum scores and waiver procedures.

The University of Minnesota Twin Cities requires international applicants and certain non-international applicants to demonstrate English proficiency. It accepts TOEFL, IELTS Academic, PTE Academic, Cambridge, and Duolingo, with alternate waiver routes and conditional admission options.

ASU requires proof of English proficiency from international undergraduate applicants or applicants whose native language is not English. ASU accepts TOEFL, IELTS, PTE, Duolingo, and Cambridge exams, with program-specific minimums and documented exemptions.

UGA states that first-year international applicants whose first language is not English can demonstrate English proficiency through SAT/ACT evidence or IELTS/TOEFL results; it also lists a qualifying U.S. college composition route.

The University of Maryland requires international undergraduate applicants to provide official English proficiency scores. It accepts Duolingo, IELTS, and TOEFL, with scores less than two years old and limited waiver discretion.

Rutgers requires an English proficiency examination for applicants whose secondary schooling was outside the U.S. where English is not the principal language. It accepts TOEFL, IELTS, MET, SAT, ACT, PTE, Duolingo, and Cambridge evidence, with campus-specific scores.

Penn State requires international students whose native language is not English to submit proof of English proficiency. It accepts Duolingo, TOEFL, IELTS, SAT, ACT, GCSE/GCE English, IB English, and qualifying U.S. schooling or coursework routes.

Michigan State publishes English proficiency requirements for undergraduate applicants and accepts TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo, SAT/ACT, MSUELT, CELP, PTE, AP, IGCSE/GCSE/A-level, and IB English evidence, including regular and provisional admission thresholds.

The University of Rochester requires international students to provide English proficiency evidence through an exam or waiver request. It accepts Duolingo, IELTS, and TOEFL and publishes recommended scores, waiver conditions, and an English support pathway.

Brandeis asks international undergraduate applicants whose native language is not English to submit English proficiency results. Its official undergraduate admissions materials list TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo, and Cambridge Assessment options.

Case Western Reserve requires applicants whose first language is not English to submit an English exam score. It accepts Duolingo, IELTS, PTE Academic, and TOEFL and publishes waiver criteria based on English-medium schooling or SAT/ACT results.

Stony Brook requires international students to provide English proficiency evidence unless they qualify for an exemption. It accepts TOEFL, Duolingo, SAT, ACT, IELTS, AP, IB, A-level, and PTE Academic results and provides conditional admission options.

The University at Buffalo requires international undergraduates to demonstrate English proficiency unless waived. It accepts TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo, PTE, SAT, and ACT evidence and lists a transfer-course waiver route.

Colorado School of Mines requires non-native-English international applicants to provide English proficiency evidence before enrollment. It accepts TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo, and Cambridge options, with additional approved routes and published score thresholds.

WPI requires international applicants to provide English proficiency evidence. It accepts TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo, and PTE with recommended scores; InitialView and Vericant are optional supplements and do not replace testing.

Stevens requires international applicants whose first language is not English to demonstrate proficiency. It accepts TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo, PTE, and SAT evidence, with published minimums and case-by-case waiver criteria.

Rensselaer requires non-native English speakers or international students with limited U.S. college study to demonstrate English proficiency through TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo, or PTE. It publishes exemptions based on academic scores and English-medium education.

Loyola Chicago may require official English-proficiency scores for international undergraduate applicants. The official page lists TOEFL, IELTS, PTE, and Duolingo as proof options, with current minimums of TOEFL 4.5 for tests taken after January 1, 2026 (79 for earlier tests), IELTS 6.5, PTE 53, and Duolingo 110. Loyola states that English proficiency is not waived based only on country of origin or medium of instruction, while AP/IB coursework may be reviewed for a waiver; conditional admission is available through ICAP.

Marquette requires international undergraduate applicants whose native language is not English to submit evidence of English ability. The official page lists TOEFL 86 total with at least 20 in each section for tests before January 21, 2026 (4.5 for tests on or after that date), IELTS 6.5 in each section, Duolingo 120, SAT Evidence-Based Reading 560, or ACT English 24 and Reading 20; certain U.S./Canadian study may satisfy the requirement.

Fordham requires English-proficiency results for international applicants whose first language is not English and who have less than four years of recent all-English instruction. The undergraduate page lists TOEFL iBT 4.5+ for scores from January 2026 (90+ before January 2026), IELTS 7.0+, Duolingo 125+, or PTE 65+. Applicants with at least four years of all-English instruction may request a waiver through the applicant portal; Via Fordham is an alternative pathway for some applicants.

Syracuse requires English-proficiency exam results for first-year and transfer applicants outside the United States whose first language is not English, subject to limited waiver review. Accepted exams include TOEFL, IELTS, Cambridge, PTE, and Duolingo. The official page publishes preferred scores by school rather than a single universal minimum; for Arts and Sciences, Maxwell, VPA, Education, Engineering and Computer Science, Falk, and iSchool it lists preferred TOEFL 85+ (4.5 under the new scale), IELTS 6.5+, Cambridge 176+, Duolingo 125+, SAT Evidence-Based Reading 600, and ACT English 27.

Boston College requires international undergraduate applicants to demonstrate English proficiency with TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo results. The official policy indicates that the requirement may be waived for native English speakers, applicants with at least three years in a U.S. high school non-ESOL curriculum, or applicants with SAT Evidence-Based Reading 650+ or ACT English 29+; the admissions catalog lists recommended scores of TOEFL 100, IELTS 7.5, or Duolingo 130.

Bucknell requires proof of English proficiency for international applicants whose native language or secondary-school language of instruction is not English. It accepts TOEFL, IELTS, PTE, or Duolingo results; the official page lists minimums of TOEFL 5 (100 before January 21, 2026), IELTS 7, PTE 68, and Duolingo 130. A waiver may be requested through a school counselor or official.

Caltech requires English-proficiency exam scores from international applicants unless English is the applicant's native language or the primary language of instruction in secondary school. It accepts IELTS, TOEFL, and Duolingo; current minimums are IELTS 7 in each area, TOEFL 5 in each area for tests on or after January 21, 2026 (100 total and 25 in each area before that date), and Duolingo 130 in each area. InitialView is recommended but does not replace the exam.

Carnegie Mellon requires official English-proficiency results for nonnative-English-speaking undergraduate applicants. It accepts TOEFL iBT or Home Edition, TOEFL Essentials, IELTS Academic or IELTS Online, Duolingo, and Cambridge English. Current requirements include IELTS 7.5 overall, TOEFL iBT 5 overall for tests on or after January 21, 2026 (102 before that date), TOEFL Essentials 11, Duolingo 135, and Cambridge 191; InitialView or Vericant interviews are recommended but not required.

Georgetown recommends, but does not require, English-proficiency test results for undergraduate applicants who attend a school where English is not the language of instruction. It accepts Duolingo, IELTS, and TOEFL results to fulfill this recommendation; the university's undergraduate international admissions page does not publish a universal minimum score for this recommendation.

Indiana University Bloomington requires all international undergraduate applicants to demonstrate English proficiency within the previous two years. Accepted routes include TOEFL 79 iBT, IELTS 6.5, Duolingo 115, Cambridge 176, PTE 53, Michigan MET 53, SAT Evidence-Based Reading and Writing 560, ACT English 21, specified IB/AP/A-level English results, qualifying English-speaking-country schooling, and IU's intensive English program.

Lehigh requires applicants to demonstrate English proficiency unless English is the applicant's first language or the last two completed years of formal instruction were in English. TOEFL and IELTS are preferred, while TOEFL Home Edition and Duolingo are considered; Lehigh describes competitive guidance of TOEFL 95+ (5.5+ on the new scale), IELTS 7.5+, or Duolingo 120+, and states SAT/ACT cannot substitute for English proficiency.

NYU undergraduate applicants whose first language is not English generally need English-language testing unless they are exempt, including applicants with three or more consecutive full academic years in an English-medium school or university. NYU states that it has no minimum language-test score, but competitive applicants typically submit TOEFL iBT 100+, IELTS Academic 7.5+, PTE Academic 70+, Cambridge 191+, iTEP 4.5+, or Duolingo 125+; the accepted tests and score guidance are published in the undergraduate bulletin.

Olin highly recommends English-proficiency results for applicants whose primary language is not English, unless they have attended an English-instruction school for at least four years. Olin accepts TOEFL iBT, IELTS, Duolingo, and PTE, with recommended minimums of TOEFL 100+, IELTS 7+, Duolingo 120+, and PTE 65+. Applicants submitting SAT or ACT scores do not also need an English-proficiency exam; applicants submitting neither SAT nor ACT must submit an English exam.

Johns Hopkins recommends, but does not require, TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo, or Cambridge English results for applicants whose primary language is not English or who have not attended an English-language school for the last three years. The official testing page gives competitive guidance of TOEFL 5 total with preferred subscores, IELTS 7.0 in each band, Duolingo 120 with preferred subscores, or Cambridge 185+; SAT/ACT is required for first-year admission.

Rose-Hulman requires international undergraduate applicants to submit proof of English proficiency as part of a complete admission application. The official international-students page accepts TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo scores; the page does not state a universal minimum score in the available admissions requirements section.

Texas A&M requires international freshman applicants whose spoken language is not English to demonstrate English proficiency. Accepted routes include TOEFL iBT 80 before January 21, 2026 or 4.5 overall with at least 4.0 in each skill on or after that date, TOEFL Essentials 8.5, IELTS Academic 6.0, SAT Evidence-Based Reading and Writing 560, ACT English 21, or completing all four years of high school in the United States; the official page also lists specified English-speaking-country exemptions.

UC Davis requires international applicants to demonstrate English proficiency when they studied in the United States for fewer than three years and received instruction in a language other than English before arriving. Accepted routes include specified AP/IB results, transferable college coursework, TOEFL, IELTS, and Duolingo; UC's systemwide first-year benchmarks include IELTS 6.5+, TOEFL iBT 4.5+ on the post-January-2026 scale (80+ before), or Duolingo 115+.

UC Irvine requires English proficiency evidence when an applicant has had fewer than three years of English instruction by high-school graduation. Accepted routes include ACT English 24, SAT Writing and Language 31 or SAT EBRW 680, specified AP/IB results, IELTS 6.5+, TOEFL iBT 4.5+ from January 2026 (80+ before), Duolingo 115+, or a qualifying UC-transferable English composition course; UC Irvine does not accept TOEFL MyBest scores.

UC San Diego requires international first-year applicants whose native language is not English and whose secondary education was not taught in English to demonstrate English proficiency. Minimums are TOEFL iBT 4.5 from January 2026 (83 before), IELTS Academic 7, or Duolingo 115; specified AP/IB English results are also accepted. Transfer applicants may use two transferable English-composition courses with grades of B or better when their instruction was in English.

UC Santa Barbara requires applicants whose native language is not English and whose secondary or higher education was not taught in English, or who have fewer than three years of English instruction, to demonstrate proficiency. Accepted routes include IELTS 6.5+, TOEFL iBT 4.5+ from January 2026 (80+ before), Duolingo 115+, specified AP/IB/SAT/ACT results, or a qualifying UC-transferable English-composition course; UCSB does not accept TOEFL MyBest scores.

For international undergraduate applicants, the University of Florida catalog states that applicants whose native language is not English must submit official TOEFL or IELTS scores. The current catalog page does not publish a universal minimum score on the freshman admission section, so no numeric threshold is inferred here.

Santa Clara requires international undergraduate applicants whose first language is not English to demonstrate proficiency. The official page lists IELTS 6.5, TOEFL iBT 90 before January 21, 2026 or 4.5 on the post-January 21, 2026 scale, and Duolingo English Test 120; qualifying SAT or ACT English scores and four years of English-medium secondary schooling are also accepted routes.

Pepperdine accepts several routes for international undergraduate English proficiency: SAT Evidence-Based Reading and Writing 600+, ACT Reading 24+, TOEFL iBT 85+, Cambridge C1/C2 186+, Duolingo English Test 120+, or IELTS 6.5+. It also lists qualifying English-medium schooling and coursework alternatives and does not accept TOEFL MyBest Scores.
